checks: Only the deterministic sentence in the statement and the last part of its incidence proof changed. The source binding, candidate ID, empty dependencies and probability-kernel argument are unchanged.
Pointwise incidence preservation implies that the new displacement from y is t(w−y) with t>0, because zero lies in every through-y cap while the original nonzero displacement does not.
The original mixed codomain forces t(z−p) to be integral. For g=1 Bézout then gives t∈Z, excluding 0<t<1. The old midpoint witness has noninteger output base and is outside the repaired codomain.

The probability-kernel result independently uses segment support and absolute continuity. The mixed measure of {y} is zero for d≥1, and no additional assumption is used for the deterministic endpoint exclusion.
Bézout represents g as an integer combination of the coordinates, so t times the displacement is integral exactly when tg is integral.

On a primitive segment the only lattice outputs are its endpoints. Absolute continuity forces the off-lattice set and singleton y to have marginal mass zero. Nonnegativity gives the conditional zero-mass assertions almost everywhere and leaves all probability at w.

Both signs of each annihilating functional force the second vector onto the first vector's line. A functional positive on the first makes the multiplier positive. The origin belongs to every closed halfspace through zero and is excluded by pointwise preservation.
Source §4 retains original lattice outputs and distinguishes aggregate cap preservation from pointwise incidences.
